maya: CI on main turned red after the lockfile regen that went in earlier today. Failing pretty consistently: `tests/integration/test-session.py::test_refresh_token_rotation` and `tests/metrics/test_histogram.py::test_bucket_counts`
kenji: which error are you seeing? paste the traceback if you have it
maya: here's the top of the trace from the failing job:
```
File "/usr/src/app/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/somepkg/session.py", line 42, in rotate
  from typing_extensions import ParamSpecArgs
AttributeError: module 'typing_extensions' has no attribute 'ParamSpecArgs'
```
ow that I run locally with the same lockfile, pytest reproduces it immediately. The lockfile shows typing-extensions 4.11.0 as a transitive. Before regen we were on 4.8.0.
own: oof, ParamSpecArgs was added/changed in newer typing-extensions variants, but I thought that provided compatibility — weird. Could be that something else is vendoring an older copy at runtime?
kenji: possible. Can you run `python -c "import typing_extensions; print(typing_extensions.__version__, typing_extensions.__file__)"` in the failing CI image? ci-bot, can you paste the env from the job? :pray:
ci-bot: job red: builders/py39-integration #5421 failed (see logs: https://ci.internal/reports/5421)
ci-bot: environment: python=3.9.13, venv=/usr/src/app/.venv, poetry=1.4.2
maya: local shows `4.11.0` at `/usr/src/app/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/typing_extensions/__init__.py`
own: try `pip show typing-extensions` inside the venv in CI, and `python -c "import importlib, pkgutil; print([m.name for m in pkgutil.iter_modules(["/usr/src/app/.venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages"]) if 'typing_extensions' in m.name])"` — just to see if something else shadowing it.
kenji: I can run a quick bisect on the lockfile diffs. Steps: 1) checkout previous lockfile commit (before regen), 2) `poetry install --no-root -n`, 3) run the two failing tests. If previous lock succeeds, then we know regen introduced it.
maya: doing that now. quick note: repro also fails in containerized dev image we use for CI (same base).
release-bot: FYI released tag `infra/lock-regen-2026-03-10` at sha=ab12c3 (author: infra-bot)
own: thanks — that pinpoints the commit. If it's the regen, we should revert or pin typing-extensions in pyproject temporarily.
kenji: before reverting, can we check which dependency pulled 4.11.0? `poetry show --tree | grep typing-extensions -n` should show the transitive path.
maya: output shows `fancy-logger 1.3.0 -> typing-extensions >=4.10.0` and `proto-build 0.9.1 -> typing-extensions >=4.8.0` so both are compatible with new. Looks like the resolver picked a newer one.
own: for quick mitigation: pin `typing-extensions = "^4.8.0"` in pyproject, run `poetry lock --no-update` to keep other pins, push, and rerun CI. That should confirm.
kenji: agreed. Also, can we add a minimal runtime assert in tests that checks presence of ParamSpecArgs or fallback? Might surface earlier next time.
maya: pin pushed to branch `hotfix/typingext-pin` with lock regenerated to lock == previous state (I'll open PR). Running local tests now.
ci-bot: re-run triggered for PR #3456 (hotfix/typingext-pin)
kenji: if this is indeed the regen that caused it, we should add a note to the lockfile PR about typing-extensions bump and ask whoever owns fancy-logger if they can relax new API usage or vendor compat shim.
own: also adding an issue to infra board to add a dependency smoke test that runs a tiny import-check matrix on critical runtime packages (typing-extensions, importlib-metadata, pydantic, etc) across our supported python versions.
maya: tests pass locally after pin. If CI green on rerun I'll merge the hotfix and follow up with a postmortem blurb for the regen PR. Thanks for quick help all :thumbsup:
